Subject: Post-demo: NovaCare next steps & eval kit

Hi Sarah / Sam —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side to help you validate fit for the clinical triage assistant use case: 

1) Eval Kit (attached): a small prompt set + conversation snippets that represent triage intents, slot extraction, and follow-up clarification flows. File: novacare_prompt_set_v1.jsonl
2) Recommended baseline models: 2x smaller LLM for high-throughput classification (redwood-llama-13b-qa-quant) and a larger model for generative follow-up (redwood-mix-70b). See benchmark links below.
3) Structured output: we recommend enforcing a JSON schema for the triage result (intent, severity_score, recommended_action, evidence_span). We included a suggested schema and two example responses in the Drive folder.
4) Tool/function calling: we propose evaluating both direct function-call (server-side) and the fallback text-parsing path. We'll measure schema compliance, parse failures, and retry performance.
5) Next steps:
   - You: confirm which subset of patient scenarios (urgent, routine, medication question) we should prioritize (suggest 50/30/20 split).
   - Us: run the Eval Kit across the two recommended model profiles, return a short results table and failure analysis within 72 hours.

Attachments: novacare_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, brief readme + link to benchmark results.

Slack / call availability: I have a 30–60 minute slot tomorrow 10–11am PT if you want to walk through the prompt set.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — great questions. Quick answers and links below, plus what we'll include in the formal run: 

- Benchmark links & raw artifacts: Drive folder (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBxyz-novacare-eval-kit — contains csvs with token counts, latency p50/p95/p99, cost estimate column, and failure reasons. I also pasted a short summary in the attached novacare_benchmark_results_link.txt.

- JSON schema handling and retries: our recommended policy for this workload is:
  1) Prompt-safety wrapper that validates the response against the target JSON schema client-side.
  2) If schema validation fails or keys are missing, we automatically attempt one context-constrained retry with an explicit "Fix JSON only" instruction and the original chat history reduced to the last 2 turns (to preserve user intent).
  3) If the retry still fails, we run a low-latency fallback to a smaller deterministic model and emit a trace event tagged "schema_fallback" so you can route for human review.

- We will include counts for: initial schema failures, retry success rate, fallback frequency, and median extra latency added by retries.

- HubSpot deal id: ND-2029-042 (added to subject line in our notes).

Planned deliverables (within 72 hours):
  - Eval summary (CSV + short report), triage confusion matrix, schema-failure sample set (10 worst cases), and recommended prompt tweaks for edge patterns.

I'll run the initial job tonight and share links as they come up. If you want the retry policy tweaked (e.g., 2 retries or a different fallback model), tell us which tradeoff you prefer — lower cost or fewer human handoffs.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Looping in some operational notes for the run and a proposed acceptance checklist we should include in the deliverable: 

- Metrics to include in the CSV: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-in/tokens-out, cost-per-call, schema_validation_pass_rate, retry_success_rate, fallback_rate.
- Provide a small prompt variants document that shows: original prompt, schema-enforcing prompt, and one "conservative" prompt that biases towards shorter outputs for lower cost.
- For structured-output evals: include a small harness that attempts 3 retry policies (0, 1, 2) and records the marginal utility of each retry (delta in schema pass rate vs added latency).
- Add a short writeup on false-positive/false-negative of severity classification with examples and suggested threshold tuning.

I'll own assembling the prompt variants and running the retry-policy matrix; Karthik can confirm the model quantization profile to use for the low-cost fallback.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Solutions (North America)
Redwood Inference
